documents.title: Night observing protocol
documents.content:
# Night observing protocol

## Arrival
At the hilltop observatory, visitors allow twenty minutes for their eyes to adapt to darkness. Use red light rather than a white torch.

## Weather
Cloud cover can prevent a useful observation even after the adaptation period. The twenty-minute period does not guarantee a visible target.

documents.title: Spectrometer operation
documents.content:
Spectrometer operation
Before each spectrometer session, run a reference-lamp calibration for ten minutes. Keep the detector cover closed during calibration. After calibration, remove the cover to collect a spectrum. Never point the instrument at the Sun.

documents.title: Soil specimen submission
documents.content:
Soil specimen submission

How much soil is required?
Send 200 grams of dry soil in a sealed sample bag.
What label is required?
Write the field code and collection date on each bag.
When is a report issued?
The laboratory usually issues a report within five business days after receipt. Complex specimens can take longer.

documents.title: Seed batch preparation
documents.content:
# Seed batch preparation

1. Chill the sealed seed packet at 4 degrees Celsius for fourteen days.
2. Sow into damp compost after chilling.
3. Keep the compost moist but not waterlogged.

Germination commonly begins two to three weeks after sowing; timing varies with temperature and seed condition.

documents.title: Sound training options
documents.content:
# Sound training options

| Session | Fee | Duration | Equipment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mixing foundations | 45 credits | Two hours | Headphones supplied |
| Field recording | 70 credits | Three hours | Recorder supplied |

Both sessions require advance registration. Mixing foundations is taught indoors. Field recording moves indoors during severe weather.

documents.title: Reed instrument care
documents.content:
Reed instrument care
After playing, remove the reed and wipe moisture from the instrument with a soft swab. Let the reed dry flat before putting it in a ventilated case. Do not use hot water or leave the instrument near a heater.
